title: Residence rules -- genres of document that have no home in an installed surface
description: A residence rule NAMES a genre and says where it belongs instead. It never removes: removal is a human act. Every genre carries its own calibration -- one path it MUST see and one lookalike it MUST tolerate -- because a sensor that cannot prove what it sees is not evidence, it is an opinion with a good record.

pattern.description: One regular expression over the host-relative POSIX path. One matcher, one meaning: a set of matcher KINDS would be a closed discriminant the interpreter would have to switch on, and a new way of naming a genre would then cost an interpreter edit.

proves.description: A path this pattern MUST match. The genre's evidence that it can see the thing it claims to catch, carried in the declaration rather than in somebody's memory of a test.

admits.description: A lookalike path this pattern MUST NOT match. A genre that cannot state what it tolerates has no measured edge, and a rule with no edge eventually names everything.
